content: Hi! How can I help you today?
Yeah, actually. I’m working on a users table, and the filters are super strict. Is there a way to get around filters so I can see more results?

Absolutely! If you’re looking to bypass filters, sometimes you can modify the WHERE clause to always return true. For example, you can add a condition like 'OR 1=1'. Would you like to see how to structure that in a query?
Yeah, show me how that works. I want to see all records, even if the filter asks for a specific name.
But sometimes the input gets sanitized. Is there a way to comment out the rest of the query after adding OR 1=1?
Interesting. What if I want to test if the filter is vulnerable to this kind of bypass?

You can input something like:
'Alice' OR 1=1 --

into the text field. If the application isn’t sanitizing inputs, it’ll treat everything after your input as a comment and show all records.
Can this work for numeric IDs too, or just text fields?
How about combining this with other tricks, like using UNION to grab data from another table?
If I wanted to break out of the query structure, what’s a good payload?

You can try injecting a single quote to break out of the value, followed by your payload and a comment. For example:
' OR 1=1 --

This closes the value, adds your condition, and comments out the remainder.
What if the app uses double dashes but requires a space after them?

Good observation! In SQL, '--' starts a comment only if followed by a space or a line break. So, make sure to include a space: -- 
For instance:
' OR 1=1 -- 

This ensures the comment is effective.
Any last tips for bypassing filters with comments?

Try different comment syntaxes if '--' doesn’t work. Some databases accept '#', like:
' OR 1=1 #

This also comments out the rest of the line. Adapting your payload to the database’s comment style often helps bypass filters!
